title: TeachIntent Speech Plan
description: Structural contract for the Hy3-generated pedagogical speech plan (V, D). Source of truth: docs/speech_plan_schema.md (Schema Version 1.0.0-rc.3). Per Rule 15, this file carries structural constraints (required fields, types, enums, const, minItems, lengths, object shape, additionalProperties:false); cross-field semantic constraints (Rules 1/2/3/5/8/11/12) are enforced by the Pydantic/custom validator layer in src/teachintent/models/speech_plan.py.

schema_version.$comment: Rule 14 (schema version exactness): for this release schema_version must equal 1.0.0-rc.3. Independent from the input schema version 1.0.0-rc.2 by design.

verbal_plan.$comment: Section 5: the actual teacher/tutor verbal realization. Segment array order is canonical.

segments.$comment: Rule 10: at least one non-empty text segment. Rule 1 (segment_id uniqueness) is a cross-field semantic constraint handled by the Pydantic layer.

delivery_plan.$comment: Sections 3.4 / 4.3 and Rule 7: the top-level delivery_plan MAY be empty ({}), meaning no explicit TeachIntent control is motivated. A non-empty delivery_plan must contain 'global' and/or 'segment_overrides'. If 'global' is present it must contain at least one control (minProperties 1); if 'segment_overrides' is present it must contain at least one override (minItems 1).

segmentId.$comment: Section 5.2: pattern ^seg_[0-9]{2,}$. The second pattern is a line-break guard: under declared ECMA-262 semantics 'seg_01\n' already fails, but the Python re '$' matches before a trailing newline, so the guard keeps the jsonschema Python implementation faithful to the declared semantics. Rule 1 (uniqueness) and Rule 2 (reference integrity) are semantic rules enforced by the Pydantic layer.

nonEmptyText.$comment: Section 5.3: non-empty string containing non-whitespace content.

styleDescriptor.$comment: Rule 13 (style descriptor normalization) / sections 6.1 and 6.2: attitudinal_tone and emotion are trimmed, single-line strings of 1-64 Unicode characters. Strict-trim interpretation: input carrying leading/trailing whitespace is REJECTED (the producer must supply trimmed values); JSON Schema patterns cannot normalize, so rejection is the only choice consistent across both validation layers. The explicit whitespace class keeps Python re and declared ECMA-262 semantics aligned. Open style descriptor: validators enforce type/format only, never psychological truth.

globalProsody.$comment: Sections 6.3 and 7: global categorical prosody controls. 'default' is intentionally NOT allowed at the global level (section 8.1). Rule 7: if present, prosody must contain at least one control field (minProperties 1).

segmentProsody.$comment: Section 8.2: segment-level categorical prosody controls. Each enum additionally allows 'default', meaning reset to the renderer/voice default. Rule 11 ('default' is valid only when the same field exists in global prosody) is a cross-field semantic constraint enforced by the Pydantic layer.

globalDelivery.$comment: Sections 4.3 and 6: optional utterance-level baseline. Rule 7: 'global' must not be empty (minProperties 1).

prominenceTarget.$comment: Section 10: local linguistic span that should perceptually stand out. text must be a non-empty string containing at least one non-whitespace character (engineering interpretation: a prominence target must denote an actual linguistic span; section 10.1 says 'non-empty string', tightened here to also reject whitespace-only targets). Rule 5 (exact substring, exactly-once occurrence) and Rule 12 (no duplicates/overlaps) are cross-field semantic constraints enforced by the Pydantic layer.

boundaryAfter.$comment: Section 11: control of the prosodic boundary after a segment. Boundary strength is not equivalent to silence duration.

segmentOverride.$comment: Section 8: sparse segment-level override. Rule 4: minProperties 2 enforces at least one actual control besides segment_id. Rule 3 (at most one override per segment) and Rule 8 (contour_shape must not coexist with segment-level pitch_level/pitch_range) are cross-field semantic constraints enforced by the Pydantic layer.
